subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should macOS Push-to-Talk get a native batch STT backend seam now, and should that seam reuse Gateway `tools.media.audio` rather than adding a separate native custom-ASR endpoint setting?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the implementation changes provider routing, credentials, microphone-audio egress, fallback behavior, and native/Gateway ownership, which require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design batch PTT seam first
options.body: Add a macOS PTT-only batch backend boundary, preserve Apple Speech as default, and route opted-in final audio through the existing media-audio/provider contract with explicit security policy.

options.title: Fold into broader custom-ASR design
options.body: Treat this as a narrow slice of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 and wait for a shared native ASR provider contract across native voice flows.

options.title: Defer native backend selection
options.body: Keep native PTT on Apple Speech for now and rely on sidecars or media-understanding plugins until the security and UX requirements are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design batch PTT seam first
recommendation.body: Add a macOS PTT-only batch backend boundary, preserve Apple Speech as default, and route opted-in final audio through the existing media-audio/provider contract with explicit security policy.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest native macOS voice feature-history signal and is already timeline-mentioned for this issue family.
